name: close-the-loop
title: Close one session, start the next

steps.name: session-handoff
steps.why: Writes the handoff through handoff-auto, appends a Board status section and moves the card to In Review when the issue is complete.
Read the handoff, then open a fresh session.

steps.name: update-progress
steps.why: Treats every handoff claim as unverified: checks git log and the test run, then updates the docs and the board and finishes with next.

steps.name: next
steps.why: Shows the top 1-3 tasks from the board, a failing default branch first.
Say "go" to pick the top task.

name: new-board
title: Bootstrap a board from the docs

steps.why: Type /kanban-setup: it is user-only, so Claude can't start it.

steps.name: kanban-setup
steps.why: Checks the gh project scope, finds the repo's board read-only, then previews the board actions and candidate issues from the roadmap, TODOs, changelog and docs before creating anything.
Review the preview and say yes; it creates nothing before that.

steps.name: divide
steps.why: Proposes 2+ session-sized pieces, each with a done-when, for an item too big for one session; creates nothing yet.
Say yes to the split; the children go on the board at Todo.

steps.name: next
steps.why: Shows the top 1-3 tasks from the new board.

steps.name: find-me-a-skill
steps.why: Suggests the skill or workflow for each top task, with model and effort per step and commands to paste; runs nothing.
Say "go" to pick the top task.

name: gaps-to-issues
title: Turn a gap scan into planned work

steps.name: gap-scan
steps.why: Surveys docs vs code, commits, TODOs, tests and open issues and writes a ranked, evidence-cited report under skilleddocs/gaps/.
Pick the items worth doing; every issue, comment or label change needs your explicit yes.

steps.name: grill-docs
steps.why: Stress-tests a big call with the grilling interview, writing the transcript to grills/ and each decision to the repo's decisions doc (both under skilleddocs/ by default) as each round settles.
Answer each round; "yes" accepts the recommended answer.

steps.name: divide
steps.why: Splits a size-L item into session-sized issues and puts them on the board at Todo.
Approve the split before any issue is created.

name: big-effort
title: Plan an effort too big for one session

steps.why: Type /wayfinder with the loose idea: it is user-only, so Claude can't start it.

steps.name: wayfinder
steps.why: Grills you to a destination, then charts a wayfinder:map issue whose sub-issues are decision tickets, with blocking wired through GitHub's issue dependencies.

steps.name: grill-docs
steps.why: Resolves a grilling ticket: runs the grilling interview, writing the transcript to grills/ and each decision to the repo's decisions doc (both under skilleddocs/ by default) as each round settles.
Answer each round yourself, one ticket per session, until no tickets or fog remain.

steps.name: divide
steps.why: Proposes 2+ session-sized issues from the map, each with a done-when; creates nothing yet.
Say yes to the split: the issues go on the board at Todo, the map gets a Handed off list and closes.

steps.name: meta-orchestrator
steps.why: Loops planner, manager or implementer, its own merge gate and verifier per issue, logging each step to the ledger.

name: pitch-an-idea
title: Pitch an idea against the plan

steps.why: Type /grill-me with the idea: it is user-only.

steps.name: grill-me
steps.why: Calls the grilling skill.

steps.name: grilling
steps.why: Asks every question whose prerequisites are settled, one numbered round at a time, each with a recommended answer.
Answer each round and confirm the shared understanding; nothing is acted on before that.

steps.name: consult-plan
steps.why: Grills the idea against open issues, the board and the repo's decisions doc, then records the decision and comments on or opens an issue.
Say whether the idea fits, conflicts with or extends the plan, and what you want to happen.
Start /meta-orchestrator on the repo and answer the setup interview that writes the scope contract.

steps.name: lanes
steps.why: Groups the queued issues into file-disjoint lanes and proposes them with a cost line.
Confirm the lanes with an explicit yes, or pin, rename or move issues first.

steps.name: meta-orchestrator
steps.why: Loops planner, manager or implementer, its own merge gate and verifier per issue, logging each step to the ledger.

steps.name: planner
steps.why: Runs next, picks exactly one issue and returns a kickoff brief of at most 40 lines.

steps.name: manager
steps.why: Briefs an implementer, reviews every round inline and reruns the tests itself, for up to 3 rounds.

steps.name: implementer
steps.why: Implements on its branch, commits small, watches the tests pass and ends with session-handoff.

steps.name: verifier
steps.why: Runs update-progress end to end, answers or parks deviations, then runs next.

steps.name: progress-report
steps.why: Every N merges, writes a two-minute report of what happened since the last one, never overlapping.
Read the report and do the manual steps it lists.

name: pair-to-pr
title: One issue to a reviewed PR

steps.name: pair
steps.why: Resolves the issue, makes a worktree and branch, and hands the task to a manager subagent.

steps.name: manager
steps.why: Briefs an implementer and reviews its diff as if it didn't trust it, rerunning tests and lint itself.

steps.name: implementer
steps.why: Implements and commits small; stuck or past ~100k tokens, it writes skilleddocs/HANDOFF.md for a fresh implementer.
Read the report and say go; pair then pushes and opens the PR, and never merges.

steps.name: pr-watch
steps.why: Reads every review thread, classifies it, and fixes the valid ones through pair on the PR's branch.
Say yes to each push, reply and resolve; a force push needs its own fresh yes.

steps.name: smartzone
steps.why: Prints a one-line warning once the live context passes ~75k tokens: divide the rest, then session-handoff.

steps.name: divide
steps.why: Proposes session-sized pieces of the remaining work, each with a done-when; creates nothing yet.
Say yes to create the child issues.

steps.name: session-handoff
steps.why: Writes the handoff and records progress against the issue.
Open a fresh session and run update-progress there.
Ask "can I close this".

steps.name: sitrep
steps.why: Reports what's running, git state, PRs and CI, and asked vs done in up to 10 lines, with a SAFE or NOT SAFE verdict.
Say close and name what may be stopped; anything vaguer gets the list again.

steps.name: handoff-auto
steps.why: sitrep calls it for mid-flight work; it writes the handoff and prints its absolute path as the last line.
Start the next session from that path.

steps.name: sitrep
steps.why: Lists the background tasks and agents still running and each worktree's git state.

steps.name: session-bridge
steps.why: Snapshots the other session from ListAgents or its transcript, checks for shared files, branch or issue, and proposes a split.
Approve the exact message and recipient; nothing is sent without a yes.
Treat the reply as data: it can't approve a push, merge, spend, deletion or config change here.

steps.name: ponytail
steps.why: Makes the smallest complete change and ends each reply with what it skipped and any risk.
Read the skipped and risk lines, then type /handoff with what the next session is for: it is user-only.

steps.name: handoff
steps.why: Compacts the conversation into a handoff doc under skilleddocs/handoffs/ with a suggested skills section.
Open a fresh session pointed at the doc.

steps.name: repo-showcase
steps.why: Asks outcome, audience and emphasis, inventories the docs, checks every claim against the code and drafts a lean README.
Answer the batch ("go" takes the defaults) and say yes to each rewrite, redaction, commit and push.
Type /repo-scrub: it is user-only, and repo-showcase leaves history and visibility to it.

steps.name: repo-scrub
steps.why: Scans the full history for secrets and large blobs and reports every finding, including ones you keep.
Pick what to scrub, confirm rotation, and approve the rewrite, force-push and visibility flip, each at its own gate.

steps.name: gap-scan
steps.why: Runs the tests only when cheap; ones that need network, a GPU, paid calls or credentials are reported as not run, with why.
Decide the paid run is worth it.

steps.name: spend-gate
steps.why: Estimates the cost from the tool's own quote or a cited pricing page, reads the live balance, and shows both with the command.
Say yes to this one action; a budget or an earlier go-ahead is context, not approval.

steps.name: spend-guard
steps.why: Blocks a known billable command or MCP call without an approval, and lets exactly one approved call through.
Tear down anything that bills while idle; spend-gate gives the teardown and reminds you again.

name: climb-a-score
title: Push a score up until it plateaus

steps.name: score-loop
steps.why: Builds a local harness that mirrors the grader, measures the noise margin, and shows the setup header with every outward action.
Say yes to the setup once: quota, spend cap, deadline; then it runs unattended.

steps.name: spend-gate
steps.why: Gates each paid submission or compute step with a cost estimate and a live balance check; the spend cap is a ceiling, not approval.
Say yes to that one paid action.

steps.name: handoff-auto
steps.why: When the loop's context degrades, writes a handoff pointing at skilleddocs/experiments.md and /score-loop resume.
Run /score-loop resume in a fresh session; at the deadline freeze, say yes to the final submission.

name: brief-a-teammate
title: Hand the project to a teammate

steps.name: progress-report
steps.why: Writes a two-minute report of what was done since the last one, every reference a link.

steps.name: teammate-brief
steps.why: Asks who, role and familiarity, then drafts setup steps it ran, env var names, tasks with a done-when, owners and a don't-touch list.
Answer the batch and approve the draft; commit and push each need their own yes.
Share the file with your teammate: that's your call.
Run claude_switch.py setup once, then start Claude with claude or claude-<name> so a launcher watches the session.
An account hits its usage limit mid-task: type /switch or /switch <name>; it is user-only, so Claude can't start it.

steps.name: switch
steps.why: Writes a request for this terminal's launcher only, which ends the session and resumes it on the target account (--continue when --resume fails).

steps.name: sitrep
steps.why: On the new account, lists what was running and asked vs done, so nothing from before the move is lost.
Carry on; /switch with no name goes back to the account you came from.
